rows.title: Scavenging for sport: How Trash Panda turns waste plastic into disc golf discs
rows.standfirst: The one for sure thing in Denver-based Trash Panda’s business plan is that the supply of raw materials is endless

rows.title: Colorado business leaders are still negative about the future economy, though less so than last year
rows.standfirst: CU business school’s quarterly survey ranked geopolitical concerns as the top reason for feeling negative about the second quarter. Also: Use of AI at work is spreading.

rows.title: This Colorado neighborhood is saving bees through sustainable development. Here’s how.
rows.standfirst: At Baseline master-planned community in Broomfield, residents support pollinators that support clean water and our food supply

rows.title: Xcel proposes new rate scale for data centers to shield consumers from added power costs
rows.standfirst: So-called large-load customers could make up most of the new demand for electricity in Xcel’s service area in 5 years. Consumer advocates say they must pay their own way.

rows.title: A dose of amino acids could give developing Western Slope peaches strength to survive deadly spring freezes
rows.standfirst: Colorado State University researchers are cautiously optimistic as they prepare to test their theory against a freeze forecast for this weekend

rows.title: What’s Working: What’s up with job openings in Colorado?
rows.standfirst: Three employers talk about jobs they’re hiring for. Plus: 3 labor strikes, Apprenticeship Month, tech jobs growth expectations and more!

rows.title: Most Colorado cities could lose access to affordable housing funding next year. Lawmakers are racing to fix it.
rows.standfirst: The problem stems from a provision in Proposition 123 that was supposed to hold local governments accountable for increasing the supply of affordable housing

rows.title: Workers plan to halt strike at major US meatpacking plant and resume negotiations
rows.standfirst: Workers at one of the nation’s largest meatpacking plants have agreed to return to work and halt a three-week strike.

rows.title: Colorado’s future Front Range passenger train has a name, and no, it’s not pronounced choo-choo
rows.standfirst: Voters who live within a few miles of the future Fort Collins to Pueblo line may be asked to approve a sales tax as soon as November

rows.title: Legislature will try again to lower homeowners insurance rates by funding hail-resistant roofs
rows.standfirst: Colorado insurance premiums have risen 65% in 5 years. Hailstorms are mostly to blame.

rows.title: Nexstar asks states, including Colorado, for $150M bond to cover damages from order slowing merger with Tegna
rows.standfirst: The antitrust case argues the merger of the parents of 9News and Fox31 in Denver gives too much market control to Nexstar, which academics describe as a “news duplicator”

rows.title: Lakewood voters strike down pro-density zoning as repeal campaign dominates
rows.standfirst: Backers of the return to single-family zoning said they feared new rules would disrupt Lakewood’s suburban character

rows.title: With cuts coming to Proposition 123, Colorado’s budget crisis is about to make its housing crisis worse
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s state budget proposal would cut $130 million from Proposition 123, with most of the money coming from programs that develop affordable rental housing for low-income families

rows.title: Colorado lost jobs and saw its labor force decline last year
rows.standfirst: Local economists had projected meager job growth in 2025. The state lost 11,700 jobs instead — the first decline since 2010 outside the pandemic losses.

rows.title: BNSF, state reach tentative deal to end 22-year wait for rail service to northern Colorado
rows.standfirst: One-time payment of around $333M will allow daily round trips between Westminster and Fort Collins, with stops in Broomfield, Louisville, Boulder, Longmont and Loveland

rows.title: Power providers make moves that are reshaping Colorado’s electric utilities landscape
rows.standfirst: Some utilities have joined a regional wholesale power market, a first for the state, and La Plata Electric quits Tri-State

rows.title: Federal Judge extends temporary restraining order slowing Tegna-Nexstar merger another week
rows.standfirst: Ruling delays decision on permanent injunction as DirecTV, Colorado and 7 other states sue to block merger

rows.title: Elon Musk’s xAI sues over Colorado’s AI antidiscrimination law, claiming it’s a threat to Grok’s free speech
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit was filed at a time when the Trump administration looks to preempt state regulation of AI models through executive fiat

rows.title: What’s Working: “Enough is enough!” Local tech and business leaders feel Colorado is losing its competitive edge
rows.standfirst: Unfriendly business policies and regulations are to blame. State economic agency points to business gains and job creation. Plus: CSU’s $1.2B impact, new engineering space in Centennial, pandemic fraud and more!

rows.title: JBS meatpackers in Greeley ratify new contract almost one month after going on strike
rows.standfirst: Beef processor JBS agreed to a wage increase that is 10 cents an hour higher than what its last offer was before talks broke down last month

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers stopped imposing new fees amid voters’ cost-of-living concerns. They’re now making them optional.
rows.standfirst: Since 2019, Democrats have passed bills imposing new fees to pay for everything from transportation projects to waste diversion initiatives. Last year, some members of the party started saying “no more.”

rows.title: Former New York Times editor: “We were caught a little flat-footed by this president”
rows.standfirst: Dean Baquet reflects on his years at the helm of the Times and the state of media ahead of his appearance at Colorado SunFest

rows.title: Elbert County effort to block Xcel’s $1.7B Power Pathway upended by the PUC
rows.standfirst: The ruling was based on a statute used just 3 times in 21 years allowing regulators to override local land use decisions on electric and gas infrastructure projects

rows.title: Ticketmaster and Live Nation had an anticompetitive monopoly over big concert venues, jury finds
rows.standfirst: The ruling isn’t expected to immediately change the cost of going to a concert, but it may force the sale of some Live Nation such as the Fillmore in Denver

rows.title: In a chaotic job market, workers change their strategies as employers hire with caution
rows.standfirst: Unemployed Coloradans are job hunting longer while some employers say they’re spending more time to pick the right person. Has Colorado returned to a more balanced job market?

rows.title: Federal judge blocks Nexstar-Tegna TV station merger until antitrust lawsuit is settled
rows.standfirst: U.S. District Court finds that DirecTV and eight attorneys general, including Colorado’s Phil Weiser, are likely to prevail in their bid to stop the merger

rows.title: What’s Working: A Colorado bill could help creatives retain more control of their work
rows.standfirst: The idea came from a Kickstarter co-founder. Plus: A new 3D home factory, more layoff warnings, and a multi-state job fair.

rows.title: In Telluride, new regulations designed to help renters are instead driving many out of town
rows.standfirst: After a lean winter that included a resort shutdown, tenants in Telluride housing chafe under new rules that tie rents to income

rows.title: In new affordability push, Colorado Democrats look to shrink the single-family home
rows.standfirst: The state House earlier this year passed two bills designed to make it easier to build houses on smaller lots

rows.title: For 2 decades, opioids flooded the San Luis Valley. Medicaid cuts now threaten the region’s recovery.
rows.standfirst: Where worlds of normalcy and addiction collide, locals cling to a sense of community and shared resources now at risk in the wake of federal budget moves

rows.title: Denver Pavilions could be the city’s next “central social district,” experts say
rows.standfirst: Echoing planning for the 16th Street shopping center in the late 1990s, an independent panel offered suggestions to shake off current economic malaise

rows.title: 1914 Ludlow Massacre took lives of 25 miners and family members during bitter strike for fair wages
rows.standfirst: Colorado voters had endorsed an amendment to the state constitution in 1902 that guaranteed an 8-hour work day, but it was not uniformly enforced.

rows.title: PNC to cut up to 777 FirstBank employees post-merger. Some have already been offered new jobs.
rows.standfirst: Those who aren’t hired by PNC are expected to leave starting June 30. Customer-facing staff are being retained.

rows.title: Colorado Tamale Act could open the door for more home kitchen entrepreneurs
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers are considering a proposal to bring DIY entrepreneurs out of the shadows with a bill that would lift the prohibition on refrigerated cottage foods, allowing up to $150,000 in annual sales

rows.title: More people started a business in Colorado last quarter than usual. They’re not all from here.
rows.standfirst: The 12.3% increase in new business filings is near an all-time record. The only time it was higher was when filing fees dropped to $1.

rows.title: Loss of electric vehicle subsidies sends Colorado car sales off a cliff
rows.standfirst: New EV sales are down 64% and plug-in hybrid sales are down 73% from last year, dragging down overall vehicle sales in Colorado by nearly 20%

rows.title: Company tied to Buc-ee’s buys land along Interstate 25, raising questions about next steps
rows.standfirst: The sale comes shortly after developers withdrew their application to build a Buc-ee’s travel center in Palmer Lake amid public opposition

rows.title: Palisade farmers take on low temperatures in a fight to save peaches from April freezes
rows.standfirst: Fruit growers on the Western Slope fought hard to protect their crops from cold weather, clear skies, still air and the notorious, deadly hard freeze

rows.title: Justice Department joins Elon Musk’s xAI in effort to block Colorado AI antidiscrimination law
rows.standfirst: The joint lawsuit argues that the law is unconstitutional and jeopardizes the United States’ position as “the global AI leader.” It comes as state lawmakers debate tweaks to the policy, set to go into effect June 30.

rows.title: What’s Working: Metro Denver is still in a renter’s market. Here’s what pushed the average rent down to 2022 levels
rows.standfirst: Rent concessions are still available for now. And not all tenants benefit from the renter’s market. Plus: If the Rockies were good, Mile High Asian Food Week and more!

rows.title: Across Colorado, people are fighting for the right to repair their stuff. Where can they go to learn how to do it?
rows.standfirst: “It’s not going to be any more broken than it already is if you try to fix it,” one sage tinkerer advises

rows.title: Liability waivers return to the Colorado Supreme Court with justices exploring the language in season ski pass agreements
rows.standfirst: The waivers were back in front of the state Supreme Court this month, nearly two years after the high court ruled the agreements cannot always shield ski areas from negligence claims.

rows.title: As AI license plate readers spread across Colorado, grassroots movements push back
rows.standfirst: While law enforcement leaders say the technology helps in their work, critics warn the same system can track people’s daily movements, raising privacy concerns

rows.title: Meandering Western history museum in Montrose is “a boy’s dream realized”
rows.standfirst: Archeologist Richard Fike’s collection of more than 500,000 Western artifacts and 28 historic structures at the Museum of the Mountain West draws more than 5,000 visitors a year

rows.title: Migrant workers who receive housing can be paid $2-$3 less per hour under new federal rule
rows.standfirst: Some Western Slope growers are taking advantage of the “downward compensation adjustment.” Others say they’ll be profitable without it.

rows.title: Exemptions to Colorado’s right-to-repair laws shot down in House committee
rows.standfirst: The bill would have allowed manufacturers to withhold repair tools from IT equipment intended for use in critical infrastructure

rows.title: License swap gives Scripps broadcasting control of TV news in Colorado Springs, Pueblo and Grand Junction
rows.standfirst: Like the $6.2 billion merger of Tegna and Nexstar, Scripps’ trade with Gray Media raises worries about market concentration
